:::{#exr-score-mean-zero}
#### Mean of the score

Let $\vX$ be continuous with density $\p(\vx \mid \param)$
for a scalar parameter $\param$.
Suppose the set of possible data values does not depend on $\param$,
and the order of differentiation with respect to $\param$
and integration over the data can be exchanged.
Show that the [score](#def-score) has mean zero.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-score-mean-zero}

The step that rewrites the derivative of $\log \p(\vx \mid \param)$ uses @exr-deriv-log-density:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{\score}
&= \int \score \, \p(\vx \mid \param) \, d\vx
&& \text{(definition of expectation)}\\
&= \int \paren{\deriv{\param} \log \p(\vx \mid \param)} \p(\vx \mid \param) \, d\vx
&& \text{(definition of the score)}\\
&= \int \frac{\deriv{\param} \p(\vx \mid \param)}{\p(\vx \mid \param)} \p(\vx \mid \param) \, d\vx
&& \text{(chain rule for $\log$)}\\
&= \int \deriv{\param} \p(\vx \mid \param) \, d\vx
&& \text{(cancel $\p(\vx \mid \param)$)}\\
&= \deriv{\param} \int \p(\vx \mid \param) \, d\vx
&& \text{(exchange derivative and integral)}\\
&= \deriv{\param} 1
&& \text{(a density integrates to 1)}\\
&= 0
&& \text{(derivative of a constant)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
